newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister warns employees on Islamist dress.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister warns employees on Islamist dress.

text.p: A cabinet member in Turkey's new government warned his ministry employees on Friday to comply with secularist laws that ban wearing Islamic-style clothing at work.
"I request our public workers to conduct themselves in line with the dress laws," Finance Minister Zekeriya Temizel said in a circular to his ministry workers.
"Those who do not comply with the laws will face disciplinary investigation," Temizel said. He demanded that women employees do not wear Islamic headscarves.
Former Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan had attempted to loosen secularist restrictions on wearing Islamic clothing in public offices.
But he resigned as prime minister last month under intense pressure from the secularist army and was replaced by secularist Mesut Yilmaz.
The finance ministry was previously controlled by the Islamist wing of Erbakan's coalition.
"Although I am newly appointed, I have not seen anybody wearing headscarves in the ministry," a ministry official told Reuters.
